approach: Since the total mass on each side of the pulley is equal, the system stays at rest, and each string tension equals the weight it directly supports.

steps.text: Add the masses on each side of the fixed pulley.
steps.equation: left side = 4 kg, right side = 3+1 = 4 kg

steps.text: Equal masses on each side mean the system has zero acceleration.
steps.why_this_step: With no acceleration, each string tension can be found from plain equilibrium instead of a full Atwood-machine equation.

steps.text: The tension in the string over the pulley, attached to the 4 kg block, supports the whole 4 kg block in equilibrium.
The tension in the string attached to the 1 kg block supports only the 1 kg block, since it hangs below the 3 kg block.
Take the ratio of the two tensions.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the system accelerates because the two sides look different, missing that 3 kg + 1 kg on the right equals the 4 kg on the left.
Taking the tension in the string attached to the 1 kg block as the same main tension over the pulley, instead of the smaller tension in the separate lower string.
